title: I Let the HOA Fine Follow Their Own Fence Height Email

parts.text: I was standing in my yard with a tape measure when the HOA president told me my fence. I am thirty-eight, tired dad, patience thin. The email from last spring said four feet in the front, six in the back, measured from soil. I had six in the back. They measured from the sidewalk, which sits two inches higher because this neighborhood was poured by optimists. The president, Craig, wore a visor indoors in his soul. "You'll take it down by Friday," he said. I said, "Your email says soil." He smiled. "Spirit of the rule." My neighbor Tasha filmed from her porch because she is done. The fine print in the portal already had a $200 draft. My kid's soccer ball sat in the grass, neon yellow, smelling like rubber and rain. I photographed the tape on soil and sidewalk. Craig said cameras were hostile. I said $200 was hostile. He posted in the Nextdoor-ish HOA forum that I was refusing community standards. Then he forwarded, by accident, an email where the board admitted sidewalk-from-soil tricks "keep people compliant." It landed in my inbox because I am on the architectural committee they forgot to remove me from after I joined in January to be a good citizen. Craig's face, when I showed him my phone, did a small crash. Tasha stopped filming. "Send that," she said. I was already hitting forward to every address in the thread, including the management company in another state.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The accidental email about measurement tricks is in my drafts-to-everyone, and the $200 is already pending.

social.video_title: They measured my fence from the sidewalk — Part 1/2
social.description: A neon soccer ball, a visor president, and an HOA thread that admitted the trick. I was still on the committee list. Would you have hit forward?

parts.text: The management company replied in forty minutes, which is a miracle in HOA years. They froze the fine. Craig called an emergency meeting in the clubhouse that smells like chlorine from the pool. I brought printed emails and the tape measure. He tried to talk about tone. Tasha talked about inches. The board voted to measure from soil, as written, and to take Craig off unilateral fine duty. He said I had embarrassed volunteers. I said volunteers should not brag about tricks in email. My fence stayed. The $200 came back. Craig still walks the sidewalk with a tape in his visor brim like a cartoon. I wave. My kid plays soccer. Sometimes the ball goes over and Craig throws it back now, which is a truce I did not request but will take. I resigned from the architectural committee with a note: I joined to help, not to hunt inches. They replaced me with Tasha. I consider that a win. The soil is still the soil. The sidewalk is still two inches of optimism. I measure from dirt, like the sentence said, and I sleep. The cheap light over the sink flickered twice like punctuation I did not ask for. He said, "Don't make this a scene." I said, "It already is."

social.video_title: The clubhouse vote put inches back on soil — Part 2/2
social.description: Forty minutes from a management company is how you know the email was bad. The soccer ball truce is optional. Would you have quit the committee?
